q: How long do demerit points stay on your record?
a: 2 years from the date of the offence
w: 1 year from the date of conviction
3 years from the date of the offence
5 years from the date of conviction
e: 2 years, counted from the offence date.
s: Demerit points stay on your record for two years from the date of the offence.

q: A G1 or G2 driver gets a warning letter at how many demerit points?
e: New drivers: 2 = warning letter, 6 = second warning letter, 9 = 60-day suspension.
s: Two or more points

q: At how many demerit points is a G1 or G2 driver's licence suspended?
e: Novice drivers: suspended at 9 points.
s: As a Level One or Level Two driver, you will have your licence suspended if you accumulate nine or more demerit points during a two-year period.

q: A new (G1/G2) driver reaches 9 demerit points. How long is the suspension?
e: 60 days for new drivers. Fully licensed drivers get 30 days at 15 points.
s: Your licence will be suspended for 60 days from the date you surrender it to the Ministry of Transportation.

q: After a new driver's 60-day demerit suspension, their points are reduced to…
e: New drivers drop to 4 points. Full drivers drop to 7.
s: After the suspension, the number of points on your record will be reduced to four.

q: At how many demerit points is a fully licensed driver's licence suspended?
e: Full licence: 6 = warning, 9 = second warning, 15 = 30-day suspension.
s: Your licence will be suspended for 30 days from the date you hand over your licence to the Ministry of Transportation.

q: A fully licensed driver gets their first warning letter at how many demerit points?
e: Full drivers: 6, 9, 15. New drivers: 2, 6, 9.
s: You will receive a warning letter recommending that you improve your driving skills.

q: How many demerit points for failing to remain at the scene of a collision?
e: 7 is the highest number of points. It's for leaving a crash scene or not stopping for police.
s: Failing to remain at the scene of a collision

q: How many demerit points for following too closely (tailgating)?
e: 4 points: following too closely, 30–49 km/h over, or not stopping at a pedestrian crossover.
s: Following too closely

q: How many demerit points for driving 16 to 29 km/h over the speed limit?
e: 16–29 over = 3 points. 30–49 over = 4. 50+ over = 6.
s: Exceeding the speed limit by 16 to 29 km/h

q: Which offence gives the MOST demerit points?
e: Failing to stop for police = 7 points. Careless driving = 6. Tailgating = 4. Red light = 3.
s: Failing to stop for police

q: Which of these is worth only 2 demerit points?
w: Failing to stop for a school bus
e: Failing to signal = 2. Not yielding = 3. Tailgating = 4. School bus = 6.
s: Failing to signal

q: Which of these does NOT add 6 demerit points?
a: Driving 30 km/h over the speed limit
w: Failing to stop for a school bus
e: 30–49 km/h over = 4 points. The other three are 6 each.
s: Exceeding the speed limit by 30 to 49 km/h

q: A novice driver is convicted of an offence worth 4 or more points. What is recorded on their demerit record for that offence?
a: Zero points; they get an escalating suspension instead
e: For novice drivers, these offences trigger escalating suspensions (30 days, 90 days, cancellation) instead of points.
s: However, the demerit points will be recorded as zero on your record, and will not be counted towards the accumulated demerit point system.

q: You get a speeding ticket in Michigan. Will demerit points go on your Ontario record?
a: Yes: offences in other provinces, New York State and Michigan count
w: Only if you were driving an Ontario rental car
Only if the ticket is over $500
e: Out-of-province points count from other provinces and territories, New York and Michigan.
s: the State of Michigan

q: How many demerit points for using a hand-held phone while driving (full licence, first conviction)?
e: 3 points for a first conviction (6 for later ones). Novice drivers get suspensions instead of points.
s: Driving while holding or using a hand-held wireless communications/entertainment device or viewing a display screen unrelated to the driving task

q: What happens when a G1 or G2 driver reaches 6 demerit points?
a: They get a second warning letter encouraging them to improve
w: Their licence is suspended for 30 days
They must retake the knowledge test
e: New drivers: 2 = warning, 6 = second warning, 9 = suspended.
s: You will receive a second warning letter encouraging you to improve your driving behaviour.

q: How many demerit points for failing to stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing?
e: 6 points and a heavy fine for a first offence.
s: Failing to stop for a school bus

q: How many demerit points for a driver who doesn't wear a seatbelt?
e: 2 points plus a fine.
s: Driver failing to wear a seatbelt

q: How many demerit points for failing to report a collision to a police officer?
e: Not reporting = 3. Leaving the scene = 7.
s: Failing to report a collision to a police officer

q: What happens if you don't hand in your licence after it is suspended for demerit points?
a: You can lose it for up to 2 years
e: Suspensions start when you surrender your licence. Failing to do so can cost you up to 2 years.
s: You can lose your licence for up to two years if you fail to surrender your licence.

q: How many demerit points for failing to slow down and move over for a stopped emergency vehicle?
e: 3 points. It also applies to tow trucks with amber lights flashing.
s: Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle

q: How many demerit points for failing to stop at a pedestrian crossover?
e: Crossover = 4 points.
s: Failing to stop at a pedestrian crossover
